cards.headline: Nvidia CEO Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy rocks company
cards.summary: Nvidia's board opened an investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman the US alleges is a Chinese spy. Trump said the FBI is looking into it. Nvidia shares fell about 4%.
cards.why_it_matters: Nvidia anchors the AI buildout and US chip export policy, so a leadership and security cloud affects markets and national security.

sources.title: Trump says Nvidia boss told him he had no idea woman he had affair with was Chinese spy
Nvidia stock falls 4% as scrutiny turns to Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
Trump says Jensen Huang ‘is definitely suffering’ as FBI probes affair with suspected spy

cards.headline: Nvidia has no clear successor if Huang steps aside
cards.summary: Analysts and commentators say Nvidia has no obvious successor to Jensen Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, raising questions about governance as the board probes his relationship with an alleged spy.
cards.why_it_matters: Nvidia is among the world's most valuable companies, so a leadership gap could ripple through index funds and retirement accounts.

sources.title: Jensen Huang affair puts Nvidia's future at risk, with no clear successor to the renowned CEO
Nvidia has no obvious successor to Jensen Huang — and that's a problem

cards.headline: Who is Alice Huang, the woman at the center of Nvidia scandal
cards.summary: Alice Huang is a former executive of Singapore-based AI computing firm Megaspeed, which has previously been probed over allegedly supplying China with Nvidia chips. The FT reports she pitched AI chip deals to investors.
cards.why_it_matters: Questions over whether Chinese intelligence sought chip access bear on US export controls and enforcement.

sources.title: What we know about the mystery woman at the center of Nvidia's spy scandal
What is Megaspeed? The Nvidia chip buyer in the spotlight after Jensen Huang’s affair

cards.headline: Wall Street has best day in seven months as tech rebounds, oil falls
cards.summary: US stocks rallied as technology shares recovered and oil slumped, with benchmarks posting their best day in seven months despite Nvidia's drop. The Dow has had three 1,000-point swings in four days.
cards.why_it_matters: Swings this large hit 401(k)s and show how sensitive markets are to AI sentiment and Iran news.

sources.title: Asian Stocks to Rally on US Tech Surge, Oil Slump: Markets Wrap
Dow sees its third 1,000-point swing in four days. Why the volatility isn’t over yet.

cards.headline: Trump says new Iran attacks 'quite unlikely' after Qatar meeting
cards.summary: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said renewed military action against Iran is quite unlikely and called the war effectively over, though he is keeping US forces posture in the region. Officials doubt a breakthrough is near.
cards.why_it_matters: The war has driven fuel and grocery prices and cost 23 US lives; de-escalation would ease prices and risk.

sources.title: Trump: New Iran attacks "quite unlikely"
Trump calls Iran war ‘effectively over’ after talks with Qatar PM

cards.headline: Massie files articles of impeachment against Hegseth
cards.summary: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, citing the Iran war under the War Powers Resolution. Trump defended Hegseth. Some Republicans privately say it could pass; Jeffries backs impeachment.
cards.why_it_matters: A House vote this week could be the first Cabinet impeachment of this term and tests congressional war powers.

sources.title: Thomas Massie files articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
Hegseth impeachment vote looms as House Republicans privately warn it could pass

cards.headline: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket freezers
cards.summary: France said Iranian Revolutionary Guard hackers took over refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites last month, spoiling food and triggering fires. The foreign minister vowed European sanctions. Iran's response was not in the articles.
cards.why_it_matters: It shows Iran's war reaching civilian infrastructure in Europe, with similar systems used in US stores.

sources.title: France accuses Iran of cyber 'sabotage' in fridge attacks
Iran was behind cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers, Paris says

cards.headline: Saudi Arabia reports new attack on East-West pipeline
cards.summary: Saudi Arabia reported a fresh attack on its East-West oil pipeline, which crosses the desert to the coast and is essential for bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.why_it_matters: The pipeline is a key workaround for Gulf oil exports, so attacks can push global crude and gasoline prices.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia reports new attack on key East-West pipeline

cards.headline: Trump alleges midterm fraud without evidence after accepting results
cards.summary: Trump questioned the integrity of the midterms on Truth Social without evidence, after earlier accepting results. Senate Democratic leader Schumer criticized the claims as a return to baseless allegations.
cards.why_it_matters: Claims about election integrity shape trust in results and the handoff of congressional power in January.

sources.title: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
Trump reverses stance, alleges fraud in recent US midterm elections

cards.headline: Jeffries won't confirm speaker votes as House GOP weighs delaying elections
cards.summary: Hakeem Jeffries said 'we'll find out' whether he has the votes for speaker in next Wednesday's vote. Ways and Means Chair Jason Smith asked House Republicans to delay Tuesday's leadership election; Senate GOP rebels seek a delay too.
cards.why_it_matters: Who leads each chamber sets the agenda on spending, immigration and oversight for the next two years.

sources.title: Jeffries won’t say whether he has votes locked up for speaker: ‘I guess we’ll find out’

cards.headline: Trump tells DHS chief to engage Democrats on immigration, no amnesty
cards.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Trump told him to work with Democrats on immigration reform but that amnesty will not happen. Fox reports some supporters object. Jeffries said Democrats will not fund Trump's deportation efforts.
cards.why_it_matters: A possible immigration deal, or a funding standoff, affects millions of immigrants and the federal budget.

sources.title: Trump tells DHS chief to work with Democrats on immigration reform, but no amnesty

cards.headline: Sullivan campaign moves to block Peltola ballot-records lawsuit
cards.summary: Sen. Dan Sullivan's campaign filed to intervene against Mary Peltola's suit seeking records of rejected absentee ballots. Sullivan's side accuses Peltola of trying to rig the system; her campaign wants the records in the razor-thin race.
cards.why_it_matters: The uncalled Alaska race could decide Senate control margins.

sources.title: Sullivan campaign files motion against Peltola over rejected absentee ballot lawsuit
Alaska Senate fight heats up as Sullivan moves to block Peltola lawsuit over rejected absentee ballot records

cards.headline: Stephen Miller takes over as chief of staff
cards.summary: Miller formally began as White House chief of staff as Congress returned. Trump held an impromptu briefing, joked about Dana White as press secretary and named WeatherTech founder David MacNeil special envoy for manufacturing.
cards.why_it_matters: The chief of staff shapes how the administration pursues executive action against a Democratic Congress.

sources.title: Stephen Miller is now chief of staff. What does that mean for Trump?
Trump announces special envoy for manufacturing

cards.headline: Supreme Court lets Big Bend border construction resume for now
cards.summary: The Supreme Court lifted a federal injunction that blocked border wall construction in Texas' Big Bend sector, allowing work to resume temporarily. Environmental groups' lawsuit continues.
cards.why_it_matters: It shows the court's emergency docket shaping immigration enforcement and land-use fights.

sources.title: SCOTUS allows Trump admin to temporarily resume border construction in Texas' Big Bend

cards.headline: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for July 2028
cards.summary: A Utah judge set Tyler Robinson's murder trial for early July 2028. Robinson, 23, is accused of killing activist Charlie Kirk in September 2025.
cards.why_it_matters: A high-profile political killing case will take nearly three more years to reach trial.

sources.title: Suspect in Charlie Kirk killing to stand trial for murder in July 2028

cards.headline: Judge clears way for Lindsay Clancy retrial on murder charges
cards.summary: A Massachusetts judge rejected a bid to dismiss charges against Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her three children in 2023, saying a retrial would not be unconstitutional.
cards.why_it_matters: The ruling lets a closely watched case on maternal mental illness and criminal responsibility proceed.

sources.title: Judge clears way for Lindsay Clancy to be retried on murder charges
Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case

cards.headline: Waymo still passing school buses after fix, feds say
cards.summary: US regulators say Waymo robotaxis kept illegally passing stopped school buses after a software recall rolled out nearly a year ago, and want more information from the company.
cards.why_it_matters: Child safety around school buses is central to public trust in driverless cars now operating in US cities.

cards.summary: Anthropic launched two models it says improve coding, reasoning and vision. The release comes as its IPO waiting period ends, letting it begin formal marketing as early as Tuesday despite last week's AI stock slump.
cards.why_it_matters: A blockbuster AI IPO would test investor appetite for the sector after a sharp selloff.

cards.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says AI data center buildout is overheating economy
cards.summary: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the data center buildout is overheating the economy and adding upward price pressure, resembling old-fashioned demand overheating.
cards.why_it_matters: It signals AI spending could keep the Fed raising rates, affecting mortgages and loans.

sources.title: Fed's Goolsbee says data center buildout 'overheating' economy

cards.headline: October CPI due Tuesday; economists expect 0.3% headline gain
cards.summary: Tuesday's October CPI report is expected to show a 0.3% headline increase and 0.2% core. A heavy slate of Fed speakers also looms, which could test the market's rotation beyond Big Tech.
cards.why_it_matters: Inflation data guides whether the Fed hikes again in December, shaping mortgage and borrowing costs.

cards.headline: Why October's jobs report was so strong
cards.summary: CNBC outlines three unexpected drivers of October's jobs report, which beat forecasts. Axios separately finds Americans are more worried about rising unemployment even as they feel more confident they could find another job.
cards.why_it_matters: Strong hiring supports wages but pushes the Fed toward more rate hikes.

cards.headline: Goldman's Solomon says AI financing remains strong
cards.summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said investor appetite for AI infrastructure remains strong despite a reset in AI stocks and political uncertainty over data centers. JPMorgan is weighing a deep discount on stuck software debt.
cards.why_it_matters: Credit availability decides whether the AI buildout continues, which affects tech jobs and electricity demand.

cards.headline: CoreWeave and Nebius halve in value ahead of earnings
cards.summary: Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius have each lost about half their value in a month ahead of earnings this week, as credit risk overshadows growth and a 'doom cycle' narrative spreads.
cards.why_it_matters: Their debt-funded growth is a bellwether for how fragile the AI buildout financing is.

cards.headline: White House 'cautiously optimistic' ahead of Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks
cards.summary: US officials said they are cautiously optimistic as Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi Tuesday and Wednesday, the first with US mediators present since February. Zelenskyy warned Russian strikes on Dnipro bridges aim to split Ukraine in half.

cards.summary: Rosneft is limiting sales to 30 litres per car in cities and 50 on highways after new Ukrainian strikes on refineries, the FT reports.
cards.why_it_matters: Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil are squeezing Moscow's economy and bear on global fuel supply.

sources.title: Russia rations petrol after new Ukrainian strikes on refineries

cards.summary: An explosion at the Habas steel plant in Aliaga near Izmir killed at least 17 people, with Al Jazeera saying a crane collapsed into a furnace. Erdogan announced an investigation.
cards.why_it_matters: A major industrial disaster in a NATO ally, with the death toll still rising.

cards.headline: Russell Brand sentenced to 10.5 years for rape and sexual assault
cards.summary: The British comedian was sentenced to 10 years and six months after conviction on one count of rape and three of sexual assault in a case brought by six women.

cards.headline: UN climate chief says fossil fuel prices spread inflation 'like a cancer'
cards.summary: Opening COP31 in Turkey, UN climate chief Simon Stiell said a fossil fuel price crisis is spreading inflation globally. Talks focus on faster electrification amid war-driven energy disruption.

cards.headline: Fervo reports $12 billion in orders for geothermal power
cards.summary: Geothermal company Fervo says it has $12 billion in orders and is targeting natural gas as drilling costs fall at its 8.4 GW resource in Utah. Separately, Anthropic bought $3.4 billion of gas turbines.

cards.headline: FDA warns GLP-1 drugs carry risk of rare 'eye stroke'
cards.summary: The FDA required drugmakers to warn patients and providers of a potential increased risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy linked to GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs.
cards.why_it_matters: Millions of Americans take these drugs, so label changes affect patients and prescribers.

cards.headline: FDA approves Bayer drug to reduce stroke recurrence
cards.summary: The FDA approved a novel Bayer drug, the first in a new class designed to prevent blood clots without raising bleeding risk, to reduce recurrence of stroke.
cards.why_it_matters: Stroke survivors face a high risk of recurrence and current blood thinners carry bleeding danger.

sources.title: STAT+: FDA approves novel Bayer drug to reduce recurrence of stroke

cards.headline: Tens of millions in Buenos Aires? Millions welcome Pope Leo XIV
cards.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated an outdoor Mass in Buenos Aires, the second stop of a 12-day Latin America tour three weeks after lung cancer surgery. He also met clergy abuse survivors and pledged stronger safeguards.
cards.why_it_matters: The first American pope's trip tests the Church's reach in Latin America and its stance on abuse.

cards.why_it_matters: It marks a sharp shift in Hungary after Orban's departure from power, relevant to EU rule-of-law disputes.

cards.summary: The Government Accountability Office found more than 17,000 F-35 parts worth an estimated $1.3 billion were missing from the program's inventory system.

cards.summary: Drone maker Neros will expand domestic production with a $450 million Pentagon loan. It is a frontrunner in a Defense Department contest for the best affordable small combat drone.
